name: Healthcare ID Baseline
description: Healthcare identifier and content hygiene, covering all 9 rules identified in the competitor parity research. Three tiers of confidence, reflected in the actions used: (1) Medicare Beneficiary Identifier gets request_access — a tight, CMS-published format; (2) NPI and medical license numbers get justify — real identifiers but with no way to validate them precisely by pattern alone; (3) the six semantic categories (disease/medication/treatment/clinical-event/biological-attribute/family-history) get warn only — these are coarse keyword/suffix heuristics standing in for what the competitor does with an NER model or LLM judge, not equivalent detection. Expect real false positives and real misses on tier 3; treat it as a starting point, not compliance-grade coverage. See docs/speakeasy-parity-gap-analysis.md for the full reasoning.

rules.name: Require access request for likely Medicare Beneficiary Identifiers (MBI)
rules.description: Matches the CMS Medicare Beneficiary Identifier format: 11 characters at fixed alphanumeric positions, using only letters that exclude visually-ambiguous S/L/O/I/B/Z, with numeric-only positions 4, 7, 10, and 11 (e.g. 1EG4-TE5-MK73, hyphens optional). Requires admin approval before proceeding.

rules.name: Require justification for likely US National Provider Identifiers (NPI)
rules.description: NPIs are 10 digits with a Luhn-style check digit computed against a fixed "80840" prefix — RE2 cannot compute that checksum, and a bare 10-digit pattern would match almost anything (phone numbers, zip+4 strings). Only fires when the digits are immediately preceded by an "NPI"-style keyword, and even then expect false positives.

rules.name: Require justification for mentions of medical license numbers
rules.description: There is no single public format for a "medical license number" — it varies by US state licensing board, and the competitor doesn't reveal what specific pattern(s) it matches. This rule only catches the phrase itself ("medical license" / "license number") followed by an alphanumeric token — closer to a keyword flag than an identifier match. Treat as a placeholder pending real requirements from a customer that needs this.

rules.name: Warn on disease or disorder mentions
rules.description: Coarse keyword list of common disease/disorder names (diabetes, cancer, HIV, depression, etc.). This is NOT clinical NER — it will miss most real mentions (any condition not on the list, any phrasing variant) and can false-positive on non-clinical uses of these words (a "cancer" support-group Slack bot, a security "HIV"-named test fixture, etc.). Logs a warning without blocking.

rules.name: Warn on medication or drug name mentions
rules.description: Suffix-based heuristic (-cillin, -mycin, -statin, -pril, -mab, etc. — common pharmaceutical naming conventions), not a drug name database. Will miss most specific drug names and can false-positive on non-drug words sharing a suffix. Logs a warning without blocking.

rules.name: Warn on treatment or diagnostic procedure mentions
rules.description: Coarse keyword list of common procedures (biopsy, chemotherapy, MRI/CT scan, dialysis, transplant, etc.). Logs a warning without blocking.

rules.name: Warn on clinical event phrasing
rules.description: Matches phrasing that typically introduces a clinical event ("diagnosed with", "admitted for", "prescribed", etc.) rather than any specific medical fact. Very coarse — will fire on plenty of non-clinical uses of the same phrasing. Logs a warning without blocking.

rules.name: Warn on biological attribute or measurement mentions
rules.description: Coarse keyword list for common vitals/lab-result phrasing (blood pressure, blood type, BMI, heart rate, blood glucose). Logs a warning without blocking.

blocked_patterns: (?i)\b(blood pressure|blood type\s*[oab][+-]?|body mass index|heart rate|blood glucose level)\b

rules.name: Warn on family medical history references
rules.description: Matches common family-history phrasing ("family history of", "mother had", "hereditary condition", etc.). Logs a warning without blocking.

blocked_patterns: (?i)\b(family history of|mother (had|was diagnosed)|father (had|was diagnosed)|sibling (had|was diagnosed)|hereditary condition)\b
